subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: When a session JSONL lock is owned by the current live gateway PID but the run or recovery owner appears stale, should OpenClaw reclaim it automatically, wait for maxHold/watchdog, or only surface in-product repair guidance?
rationale: The code can mechanically reclaim more locks, but the safe boundary between recovering a wedged session and cutting off an active transcript writer is a maintainer policy decision.

options.title: Define a bounded live-holder reclaim policy
options.body: Allow reclaim after owner/run evidence proves the holding operation is stale, then add focused unit and packaged restart/recovery proof.

options.title: Keep live OpenClaw locks conservative
options.body: Preserve current no-reclaim behavior for live OpenClaw owners and add stronger status/doctor/in-product recovery so users are not forced into manual file deletion.

options.title: Close under broader lifecycle design
options.body: Move all remaining work to a broader run-lifecycle tracker only after confirming that tracker is open and explicitly owns same-PID session lock recovery.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded live-holder reclaim policy
recommendation.body: Allow reclaim after owner/run evidence proves the holding operation is stale, then add focused unit and packaged restart/recovery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest repeated history in the session-write-lock hardening path and is the best routing candidate for the live-holder policy boundary.
